summary: Carroll County groundhouse lookout on Middle Sister above Chocorua; in use until 1948; stone foundation remains on White Mountain National Forest land.

facts.design: Groundhouse: the lookout cabin was built on the ground, not on top of a tower
facts.status_note: The lookout structure is gone; the stone foundation remains.

access.note: Reached along the Middle Sister Trail on White Mountain National Forest land

visit.trail_note: The foundation is on the summit of Middle Sister, along the Middle Sister Trail

events.note: Chocorua Lake account: Charles Howard Walker built a stone fire tower on Middle Sister; other sources date operation from 1927
Lookout duties moved here from the summit of Chocorua; ScenicNH dates operation from 1927
ScenicNH update: the Forest Service radio repeater was removed from inside the foundation

evidence.supports: Middle Sister is one of the Three Sisters just below Mount Chocorua
evidence.quote: one of three sub-peaks known as the Three Sisters that are situated just below that famous summit

evidence.supports: Site is along Middle Sister Trail, near Mount Chocorua, in Albany
evidence.quote: along Middle Sister Trail, near Mount Chocorua, in Albany, New Hampshire

evidence.supports: Groundhouse design: cabin on the ground, not on a tower
evidence.quote: A groundhouse fire tower differs from a typical fire tower in that the lookout cabin is built on the ground, not on top of a tower.

evidence.supports: Walker built a stone fire tower on Middle Sister in 1921
evidence.quote: In 1921, Charles Howard Walker, a noted local architect, built a stone fire tower on the Middle Sister Peak.

evidence.supports: The 1921 stone structure replaced the fire stand on Chocorua
evidence.quote: replaced the fire stand on the summit of Mount Chocorua

evidence.supports: Lookout duties moved from Chocorua to this site in 1927
evidence.quote: 1927: The lookout duties were removed from Mt Chocorua to this site.
In operation from 1927-1948, the Middle Sister Groundhouse is a fire lookout tower located on Middle Sister Mountain
1948: The lookout ceased being used for lookout purposes.

evidence.supports: Later use to house radio repeater equipment
evidence.quote: It was later used to house radio repeater equipment.

evidence.supports: A Forest Service radio repeater was inside the foundation

evidence.supports: Repeater removed from the foundation by 2019
evidence.quote: Update 2019: Since the writing of this blog article, the Forest Service radio repeater has been removed from the inside of the foundation.

evidence.supports: Foundation remains intact; odds and ends at the site
evidence.quote: Today, the foundation remains intact and some odds and ends linked to the groundhouse can be found at the site.

evidence.supports: Stone foundation remains intact; odds and ends at the site (Chocorua Lake)
evidence.quote: Today, the stone foundation remains intact and some odds and ends linked to the groundhouse can be found at the site.

evidence.quote: The remains of an old fire tower, in operation from 1927-1948, can be found on the summit of Middle Sister

evidence.quote: New Hampshire - Carroll County - White Mountain National Forest

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the lookout as Ground type, Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Chocorua Lake dates a stone fire tower on Middle Sister to 1921 (Walker); the Eastern US Lookouts page and ScenicNH date lookout duty or operation from 1927. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.

sources.title: Middle Sister and the Carter Ledge Trail

Why the Summit of Mount Chocorua is Bare

notes_for_editor: Start date conflicts: 1921 (Chocorua Lake, Walker stone tower) vs 1927 (Eastern US Lookouts, ScenicNH). No staffing or fire records found, so none are in the story. Brief's kind 'ground', county Carroll and agency WMNF all check out. Elevation differs between sources (3,340 vs 3,354 ft) and is not used. Visited nothing; no photo finds. NH Division of Forests and Lands PDF on lookout history returned HTTP 403.
